title: Fourth Update on Whole-of-Government Response to COVID-19
what_it_is: Fourth Update on Whole-of-Government Response to COVID-19

sections.label: COVID-19 cases and clusters
sections.summary: Singapore confirmed 61,378 COVID-19 cases with 31 deaths, and several clusters appeared in the last two weeks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: To date, we have confirmed a total of 61,378 cases of COVID-19 infections, and 31 of them have passed on.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Locally, after half a year of low community cases, we have seen several clusters of infections over the last two weeks – a cluster involving an ICA officer and his family members, one at Tan Tock Seng Hospital (TTSH), another at Tuas South Community Care Facility (CCF), a cluster at Pasir Panjang Terminal and, most recently, a cluster at our airport terminals.

sections.label: B.1.617.2 variant in clusters
sections.summary: Sequencing showed the TTSH, ICA and Tuas South CCF clusters were driven by the B.1.617.2 variant first detected in India.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Sequencing results indicate that the recent clusters at TTSH, ICA and Tuas South CCF were driven by the B.1.617.2 variant that was first detected in India.

sections.label: First TTSH cluster case
sections.summary: The first case of the TTSH cluster was confirmed on 28 April.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: The first case of the TTSH cluster was confirmed on 28 April.

sections.label: TTSH cluster quarantine and testing
sections.summary: As of 10 May 2021, about 2,500 were quarantined, 12,500 tested, and 43 cases confirmed in the TTSH cluster.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: In total, as of 10 May 2021, close to 2,500 individuals had been quarantined; 12,500 individuals had been tested as part of the special testing operations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: A total of 43 cases were confirmed, comprising 10 staff, 26 patients and seven visitors or household members.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Of the 43 COVID-19 cases in the TTSH cluster, seven staff and two patients had received full doses of the COVID-19 vaccine.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Of the 34 individuals who were not fully vaccinated, six required oxygen, two are in intensive care and one has, sadly, passed away from COVID-19 complications.

sections.label: Vaccination doses administered
sections.summary: As of 9 May, about 1.8 million individuals received at least one dose and about 1.2 million completed full vaccination.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: As of 9 May, about 1.8 million individuals have received at least one dose of the vaccine and of which about 1.2 million individuals have received their second dose and completed the full vaccination regimen.

sections.label: Pfizer vaccine asymptomatic infection study
sections.summary: A study published in Lancet found Pfizer vaccines can reduce risk of asymptomatic infection by 91%.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: For example, based on a study published in Lancet, Pfizer vaccines can reduce risk of asymptomatic infection by 91%.

sections.label: COVID-19 re-infection cases assessed
sections.summary: As of 10 May 2021, 26 cases were assessed as re-infections, with investigations into waning immunity or lack of cross-protection against variants.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: As of 10 May 2021, 26 cases have been assessed to be re-infections.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: We are still investigating whether these are due to the general waning immunity over time or the lack of cross-protection against specific variants of COVID-19 that the individual is naïve to.

sections.label: Pfizer and Moderna age approvals
sections.summary: Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna are approved only for persons aged 16 and 18 years old and above, respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Pfizer-BioNTech and Moderna are currently only approved for use in persons aged 16 and 18 years old and above, respectively.

sections.label: Suspected adverse events reports received
sections.summary: As of 18 April 2021, HSA received 2,796 suspected adverse event reports, 0.13% of doses administered, mostly non-serious.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: As of 18 April 2021, HSA has received 2,796 suspected adverse events reports associated with the use of COVID-19 vaccines.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: This represents 0.13% of doses administered but the majority are non-serious adverse events.

sections.label: Applications reviewed and rejected
sections.summary: Of 75 applications reviewed, 45 were rejected and 30 met qualifying criteria per the independent clinical panel.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Of the 75 applications reviewed so far, 45 applications have been rejected and 30 applications were assessed by the independent clinical panel to have met the qualifying criteria.

sections.label: Advance purchase agreements and Sinovac
sections.summary: Singapore entered advance purchase agreements with companies including Moderna, Pfizer-BioNTech and Sinovac, took delivery of Sinovac, and HSA is evaluating it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: As part of our efforts to secure a diversified vaccine portfolio to improve our chances of securing a suitable vaccine that is safe and effective for our population, we entered into what we call advance purchase agreements (APAs) with several pharmaceutical companies, such as Moderna, Pfizer-BioNTech and Sinovac, last year, even before these vaccines completed their clinical trial.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: Based on the schedules that had been planned for and committed under the advance purchase agreement with Sinovac, Singapore has taken delivery of a shipment of the vaccine.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: HSA is currently carefully evaluating Sinovac and a few other vaccines for use in Singapore and we will update the public when we have made progress.

sections.label: Legislative levers against misinformation
sections.summary: When needed, legislative levers such as POFMA Correction Directions will be used to stop misinformation and fear-mongering.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: When the situation calls for it, we will also not hesitate to use legislative levers, such as POFMA Correction Directions, to stop individuals from spreading misinformation and fear-mongering.

sections.label: COVID-19 fight and MOH handover
sections.summary: The fight against COVID-19 will continue, and the speaker will hand over MOH while co-chairing the Multi-Ministry Task Force.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: With the pandemic still raging in many parts of the world, our fight against COVID-19 will continue for a while yet.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Health (Mr Gan Kim Yong)
sentences.text: I will be handing over MOH to Minister Ong Ye Kung shortly but I will continue to co-chair the Multi-Ministry Task Force together with Minister Lawrence Wong and Minister Ong.

sections.label: Education Ministerial Statement and clarifications
sections.summary: The Minister for Education will make a related Ministerial Statement, and Members may raise clarifications on both Statements.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: The Minister for Education will be making a related Ministerial Statement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: I will allow Members to raise points of clarifications on both Statements after this Statement.

sections.label: New variants spreading faster
sections.summary: New variants are spreading faster than vaccinations worldwide and are more infectious, virulent and vaccine-resistant.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: New variants are spreading faster than the current pace of vaccinations worldwide.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: These variants are more infectious and potentially more virulent and more resistant to the current vaccines.

sections.label: Vaccination rates for aviation, maritime, SHN
sections.summary: Vaccination rates are above 90% for aviation and maritime and 85% for SHN facilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Vaccination rates are now above 90% for aviation and maritime; and 85% for the SHN facilities.

sections.label: Tighter 21-day SHN regime
sections.summary: A tighter 21-day SHN regime applies to travellers from higher risk countries, who serve SHN in dedicated facilities.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But variant or not, there is always a very small tail risk of such long incubation cases.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why we have moved recently to a tighter 21-day SHN regime for travellers from all higher risk countries during this period of heightened alert.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: At this stage, we prefer to take a more cautious approach and have all travellers from higher risk countries serve the SHN in dedicated facilities.

sections.label: Entry restrictions from India and South Asia
sections.summary: In April entry approvals from India were reduced, then all travellers from India were banned, extended to South Asia in May.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: In April, we reduced entry approvals for long-term pass holders and short-term visitors from India.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Later, we moved to ban all travellers from India.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This ban was extended to the entire South Asian region from the start of May.

sections.label: Daily arrivals stable at 1,200
sections.summary: Between December and March this year, arrivals were stable at about 1,200 per day.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Between December and March this year, the figure has been stable at about 1,200 arrivals per day.

sections.label: Work Permit Holder rebate increase
sections.summary: The rebate for each Work Permit Holder will rise from $90 to $250 per month, and work with CMP employers continues.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: The rebate for each Work Permit Holder will be increased from $90 per month to $250 per month.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We will also continue to work with the CMP employers to find safe ways to bring in workers to alleviate the manpower shortage.

sections.label: Tightening rules pre-emptively
sections.summary: Unsure of hidden community cases, rules were tightened pre-emptively to reduce movement and social contacts and curb spread.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But we could not be sure if there were still hidden cases out there in the community.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: That is why we have decided to tighten the overall rules pre-emptively – to reduce our movement and social contacts more generally, so that we can reduce the risks of transmission and curb any further spread of the virus.

sections.label: Strengthened testing and tracing capabilities
sections.summary: Capabilities have strengthened: about 35,000 swabs daily, lab capacity up to 73,000, wider TraceTogether and SafeEntry, and most older and frontline workers vaccinated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: But compared to a year ago, our capabilities have significantly strengthened.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We tested about 35,000 swabs per day in the past week and have the lab capacity to test up to 73,000 per day, or even more, with pooled testing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Trace Together and SafeEntry are now more pervasive, which means we can contact trace and ring-fence cases more quickly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We are also regularly testing persons in higher risk settings and undertaking surveillance testing for symptomatic individuals, which was how we uncovered many of the cases reported over the recent days.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: We have not vaccinated everyone yet but we have covered most of our older population as well as our healthcare and frontline workers at the air and sea ports and our SHN hotels and dormitories.

sections.label: Supporting frontline workers
sections.summary: Frontline workers are thanked and urged to keep spirits up, while the public is asked to take measures seriously, get vaccinated and avoid falsehoods.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: It has been very tough for all of them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, to them, we say, "Thank you, keep your spirits up and all of us are behind you every step of the way."   The best way to support our frontline workers is to take all the prevailing measures seriously – do our part to reduce the risks of transmission and, when vaccination is offered to you, take it up as soon as possible.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Avoid spreading falsehoods or unverified information that can cause needless fear or foster divisions and suspicions in our society.

sections.label: No place for discrimination
sections.summary: As a global pandemic, there is no place for discrimination, racism or xenophobia in Singapore, and Singaporeans should complete the race together.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: This is a global pandemic – the virus and its variants are out there everywhere in the world.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, there is no place for discrimination, racism or xenophobia here in Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Yes, we have had our share of setbacks, but we have learned and we have bounced back from them.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: Importantly, we have seen the Singapore spirit shine brightly throughout these challenging times.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Education (Mr Lawrence Wong)
sentences.text: So, let us draw confidence from what we have been through; let us brace ourselves for the rest of the marathon, complete the race together and emerge stronger at the finish line.

sections.label: Help for affected TTSH workers
sections.summary: An MP asks what is being done to help affected TTSH workers with accommodation, transport and childcare.

sentences.speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
sentences.text: Can I ask the Ministers what is being done to help affected TTSH workers: nurses who cannot find a place to stay, healthcare workers who cannot find a Grab or a taxi to bring them to the hospital or to take them home after a shift; families which have been separated by necessary COVID-19 precautions who need help with childcare, help with getting the kids to continue in school?

sections.label: Hotel accommodation for healthcare workers
sections.summary: Hotels have been arranged to provide accommodation alternatives for affected healthcare workers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: In fact, we have moved in to arrange with hotels for accommodation, to provide alternatives to these healthcare workers who have been affected.

sections.label: Other drugs tested by HSA
sections.summary: A question asks what other drugs are being tested by HSA.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: First, what other drugs are being tested by HSA?

sections.label: Vaccination cost and jab expiry
sections.summary: A question asks the all-in cost for each vaccination given, noting jabs will be one year old soon.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: Soon, for those of us who have had our jabs, one year will be up.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: And the third supplementary question is, I would like to know what is the all-in cost for each vaccination that is given.

sections.label: Someone must pay consequences
sections.summary: Everyone must expect consequences, and somebody has to pay for all this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: All of us, whether in Government, business and public, consumers, we need to expect that for all these, there are consequences; that the end of the day, somebody has to pay for all this.

sections.label: Vaccine supply still limited
sections.summary: The vaccines continue to be limited in supply.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Indeed, the vaccines continue to be limited in supply.

sections.label: Vaccine portfolio beyond three brands
sections.summary: The portfolio of vaccines being studied is diversified beyond Pfizer-BioNTech, Moderna and Sinovac.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: As to what other vaccines are being studied, we have a diversified portfolio beyond Pfizer-BioNTech, Moderna and Sinovac.

sections.label: Booster jab operational plans
sections.summary: Operational plans are being drawn up to deliver booster jabs if they become necessary.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: I understand that some Singaporeans are anxious and want to know, should the booster jab be required, what we need to do about it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: So, the operational plans are being drawn up and we will be able to deliver booster jabs, if it becomes necessary.

sections.label: Rough vaccine regimen cost
sections.summary: The speaker says it roughly costs about $100 per vaccine per regimen, including peripheral costs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Roughly, it may cost about – and this is off the top of my head and I need to verify that – off the top of my head, roughly, it costs about $100 per vaccine per regimen and that it will include some of these peripheral costs and so it is not cheap.

sections.label: Racial incidents and social media posts
sections.summary: The tension appears fanned by false or misleading social media posts, and clarification is sought from the Minister for Home Affairs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: The tension appears to be fanned by posts with false or misleading narratives in the social media and circulated through WhatsApp and other platforms.

sentences.speaker: Mr Murali Pillai (Bukit Batok)
sentences.text: I seek clarification from the Minister for Home Affairs for his assessment of the security situation arising from these racial incidents connected to the pandemic.

sections.label: Man's attack on woman
sections.summary: The man shouted a racial slur, and after she said "God bless you" and walked away, he kicked her chest.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: The man then shouted at her again, used a racial slur, and she responded to him, "God bless you" and began to walk away.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: She said that the man then ran towards her and landed a "flying kick" on her chest, causing her to fall.

sections.label: Racist conduct pending investigations
sections.summary: Investigations are needed before conclusions, but the conduct appears racist if the facts are as stated.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: Investigations need to be done before we can come to any conclusions.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But such conduct, unfortunately, is consistent with some of the other things that have been happening and, if the facts are as stated by the lady, then it appears to be racist conduct.

sections.label: Racism and xenophobia warning
sections.summary: MOM has taken steps against bad practices, but parties are stoking fears and encouraging racism and xenophobia, which is dangerous for Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: MOM has taken steps to deal with these bad practices.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: But what has been happening also is that parties have been deliberately stoking the fears, encouraging racism, xenophobia and dog whistling, much like what we have seen in the US.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: That is dangerous and dangerous for Singapore because, first, it will be expatriate Indians, then it will come to Singaporean Indians.

sections.label: Invitation to debate CECA
sections.summary: Anyone who believes CECA is a problem is invited to put up a Motion to debate it openly.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: If anyone here believes that CECA is a problem, put it up for a Motion, debate it openly and let us hear whether Singaporeans benefit or lose from it.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Home Affairs (Mr K Shanmugam)
sentences.text: I invite you to put up a Motion to debate CECA.

sections.label: Allergic reactions and second vaccine
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether exclusion applies to all allergic reactions or only anaphylaxis, and what adverse events rule out a second vaccine.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Can I confirm that this applies to all allergic reactions or is it only to anaphylaxis?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And what kind of adverse events will rule out patients from taking the second vaccine?

sections.label: Anaphylaxis excludes vaccination
sections.summary: Generally, a person with anaphylaxis will be excluded from the vaccination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Generally, if you have anaphylaxis, you will be excluded from the vaccination.

sections.label: Hospital contingency plans and Tan Tock Seng
sections.summary: Hospitals have contingency plans and will continue seeing patients; Tan Tock Seng Hospital needs time to ascertain no underlying transmission before reopening to new patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Mr Giam also asked about our contingency plan for hospitals if there are cases where clusters are found.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: They all have a contingency plan and they will continue to see their patients.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: What we want to do with Tan Tock Seng Hospital is because the clusters are big and we need time for us to ascertain that there are no other underlying transmission of infection within the hospital before we reopen the hospital for new patients.

sections.label: Changi Airport cluster lessons
sections.summary: The speaker asks what lessons are learnt from the developing Changi Airport cluster and its impact on the Shangri-La Dialogue and World Economic Forum.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: We know that Changi Airport Terminal has a cluster and it is developing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
sentences.text: So, what are the lessons learnt from the clusters as they are developing in Changi Airport and what impact does it have on the upcoming Shangri-La Dialogue and the World Economic Forum that are to be held in Singapore?

sections.label: Vaccine injury claim applications
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether the 30 qualifying applications will be paid and why 75 were rejected despite doctor certification.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Earlier, he said that there were 104 applications received and about 30 applications were adjudged to have met the qualifying criteria.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, does that mean that these 30 claims are going to be allowed and some payment is going to be made on these 30 claims?

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Then, he also mentioned that there were 75 that were rejected.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I would like him to clarify the reasons for rejection because, from the portal for submission of the application, it appears that every application has to be accompanied by a doctor's certification that the side effect is related to the vaccination.

sections.label: Gym patrons bringing own equipment
sections.summary: The speaker asks if the Government will review the requirement for patrons to bring their own equipment to gyms and fitness studios.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: But I understand that this has been accompanied by a requirement that the patrons have to bring their own equipment to the fitness studios or the gyms, which, to most people, would be a disincentive to go to the place in the first place because these are things you go to the studio for because you cannot do them at home.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, I would like to ask him whether the Government will review this requirement because it is already setting capacity limits, it is saying that the activities have to be low intensity, masks have to be on at all times.

sections.label: Rejected claims and panel assessment
sections.summary: The speaker says the number is not 75 rejected and that some cases failed because severity did not meet the mark.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: There is an impact on our gym here in Parliament as well.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: That is the number; not 75 are rejected.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Among those that were rejected, some of them, the panel will have to assess whether it is more likely to be associated with vaccination or not.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: There is also a balance of probability that they have to assess.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: And some cases did not qualify because the severity did not meet the mark of a severe reaction.

sections.label: Gym closure during heightened alert
sections.summary: The speaker says gyms are high-risk enclosed spaces, so activities were stopped temporarily, but lower-risk pivots may be allowed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Because in a gym fitness centre, it is an enclosed space, many people are there, very often without masks on, spreading a lot of droplets each time you are exercising, shouting or whatever you are doing in the gym, Zumba or whatever that lesson is, the chances of a spread within that environment is very high.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: That is why we have decided, during this period of heightened alert, this is one of the highest risk kinds of activities; better to put a stop to it temporarily.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: But if the operators are able to pivot or do something differently, something of lower risk, then we will be able to allow it.

sections.label: Airport worker vaccination numbers
sections.summary: The speaker states there are 46,000 airport workers, 26,000 high-risk, and over 80% of the outer ring had at least one dose.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: At the airport, in total, we are talking about 46,000 workers; 26,000 are what we consider more high-risk.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Then, there is an outer ring that does not come into direct contact but we, nevertheless, consider them exposed to some risk.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: And for that group, more than 80% have had at least one dose.

sections.label: Testing the wider ring
sections.summary: The speaker says the wider ring who could have been affected are being put through testing, with several thousand in a one-time operation.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: Second is the wider ring, who could have been affected; put them all through testing.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: So, today, we are putting several thousand through a one-time special operation.

sections.label: Faster testing methods considered
sections.summary: The speaker says faster antigen and breathalyser tests could be interspersed with PCR tests every 14 days, pending discussion with the Minister for Health.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: One thing we can possibly do – and I have to discuss this with the Minister for Health, besides the PCR test once every 14 days – is how can we intersperse it with something like the antigen test, something faster?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Transport (Mr Ong Ye Kung)
sentences.text: We are also developing a breathalyser test, something that can pick up quickly even though it may be less accurate.

sections.label: Vaccinating younger population
sections.summary: If results deem it effective and safe, the vaccination programme will be rolled out to the younger population shortly.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: Once the results are out and if it is, in fact, deemed effective and safe for deployment to the younger population, we will roll out the programme to vaccinate the younger population, also shortly.

sections.label: Re-opening plans if cases curbed
sections.summary: If current community cases are curbed and things return under control, there is a chance of getting back on track with re-opening plans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: Assuming we are able to curb the current community cases, bring things back under control, yes, I think there is a chance we will be able to then get back on track with our re-opening plans.

sections.label: Vaccination and re-opening plans
sections.summary: Crossing 50% vaccination means clusters would infect fewer people, and staying vigilant while pressing on with vaccination could keep re-opening plans on track.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: The more we do so, for example, once we cross 50% of the population getting vaccinated, all the models and all the studies suggest that then, even if a cluster were to happen, the number of people infected will not be as large.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: It would be more contained and we will be safer.

sentences.speaker: Mr Lawrence Wong
sentences.text: So, if we stay alert, stay vigilant, uphold all the prevailing safe management measures, continue to press forward with our vaccination programme, then I think there is a good chance we can remain on track with our re-opening plans.

sections.label: No place for racism
sections.summary: The speaker agrees with the Minister for Home Affairs' statement that there is no place for racism in Singapore, with no exceptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Insofar as the Minister for Home Affair's statement is concerned, indeed, we are in agreement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There is no place for racism in Singapore – no "ifs", no "buts".

sections.label: Infographic for vaccination messaging
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to consider turning a useful document into an infographic for sharing, especially for the hard-to-reach 20% to 25%.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: As usual, when you are concerned, you tend to be more animated and this can take on a life of its own.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: So, my request to the Minister is to consider whether this very useful document can be made into an infographic for easy sharing amongst members of the public, particularly the last 20% to 25 % that Minister said is hard to get through to with regard to the messaging on vaccination.

sections.label: Tan Tock Seng visitation hours
sections.summary: The Tan Tock Seng Hospital cluster severely curtailed visitation hours for family members of some patients, and the Ministry is asked to consider a regime for more face time.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: And the cluster at Tan Tock Seng Hospital has resulted in the visitation hours for family members of some of these patients to be severely curtailed.

sentences.speaker: Mr Pritam Singh (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I am requesting the Ministry to consider whether there could be some regime to help these family members to have a bit more face time with their ill or terminally-ill family members.

sections.label: Exceptions for terminally ill visits
sections.summary: Family members wanting to visit elderly, frail or terminally ill loved ones can have exceptions made by the hospital, or appeal to the hospital or the speaker.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: But we do understand that there are family members who want to visit their elderly, their frail loved ones, particularly those who are terminally ill.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: They want to spend time with them and the hospital will make exceptions.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gan Kim Yong
sentences.text: And if you do come across any of these cases, you can either appeal to the hospital or to me.
